Rent Party is a property-trading party game for friends and family. Take on friends online or around one phone, or play CPU characters offline, then pause any game and pick it up days later. You roll two dice, buy the unowned streets you land on, trade for full color sets, and build houses and hotels so the rent on your streets keeps climbing. The game runs the bank. The last player who isn’t bankrupt wins.

Online. Live tonight, or one turn at a time over days. Online play needs an account: sign in with Google to start or join a room. Online play covers rooms, invites and timers. Pass-and-play. 2 to 8 people, one phone or tablet, one crowded couch. Each time the phone changes hands, a hand-off screen keeps your trades and auction bids private. No account, no internet, no peeking. CPU characters. Rivals with names, personalities and opinions, on Easy, Normal, Hard or Expert. No account, no signal, and every move saves on your device. Meet the rivals.
documents.s: Three ways to pull up a chair

documents.t: Open Start a game and pick your kind of game night: Online, Pass-and-play or CPU characters. Players. Who’s at the table? 2 to 8 players, up to 5 of them CPU characters. Every seat gets a name and a token. Board. Kettleford comes with the game. The others are earned with coins in the shop. Every board plays by the same rules. House rules. Pick a preset or switch rules on one at a time. House rules lists them all. Ready to roll. Check the summary, then choose Start game. For an online game, the last step is Create room, and your friends join with a game invite. Got a room code or an invite link? Put it under Join a room on the Start a game page and take your seat.
documents.s: How do you start a game?

documents.t: No. Pass-and-play and CPU games work without one, and they’re saved on this device. Sign in with Google to play online, keep cloud saves and earn coins. Your account covers what signing in adds.

Rent Party runs in a current browser on phones, tablets and computers, iPhone and iPad included, with the same game, the same account and the same table everywhere. It isn’t in an app store yet. Once you’re signed in, your games follow you from screen to screen. In your phone’s browser it’s laid out like an app. On a computer you get the full board, with room for your deeds. When the Start a game page offers Install Rent Party, choosing Install adds it to your home screen, so you can start pass-and-play or CPU games offline in one tap. On iPhone or iPad, tap Share, then Add to Home Screen.

The rules, top to bottom, before game night. Online play, to get the crew back at one table. Pausing a game, for when life calls. Help and FAQ, when something doesn’t look right. Rather learn by playing? Practice against a CPU character.
Your seat follows you. Sign in with Google to play online, keep cloud saves and earn coins. Pass-and-play and CPU games work without signing in, and they’re saved on this device.

Choose Sign in and pick your Google account. Google is the only sign-in, so there’s no Rent Party password to forget. Google opens in its own window. If your browser blocks it, allow pop-ups for the site, then try again. On another device, sign in with the same Google account and your online games, cloud saves, coins and collection are waiting.

A short setup follows your first sign-in, and you can skip any step for now: Your name. What should the table call you? It shows on the board, in chat and on your public card. Your token. It walks the board for you. More tokens wait in the shop, for coins you earn by playing. Notifications. Turn them on to hear when it’s your turn, when you’re invited and when the table votes on a pause. An invite code. A friend’s invite code counts if you enter it within an hour of signing up.

Your display name, avatar, stats and badges, the token, board, dice and frame you have equipped, and a link to your public card. Everyone sees your display name. The leaderboard is off until you switch it on. The leaderboard then shows your display name, token, rating, rank and number of rated games to anyone, signed in or not. Your games count toward your rating either way.

Every alert lands in your Inbox: turn alerts, invites and plan news. From there, three settings decide what else reaches you, under Settings, Notifications. Setting What it does Push notifications Your turn, invites, pause votes and results, on every device you allow. Quiet hours Alerts wait until quiet hours end. Game clocks don’t stop, so your turn timer keeps running. Quiet hours and dates follow your time zone. Email Game alerts don’t come by email. They land in your Inbox, and on push if it’s on. This switch covers Family invites and news from the team. Payment, plan, support and deletion emails always arrive. If notifications are blocked in your phone’s or browser’s settings, allow them for Rent Party there, then come back. Why didn’t I get an alert? covers the rest.

When a friend opens a room for friends, it’s listed for you on Play online. Blocking someone ends your friendship. You won’t see each other’s chat, and neither of you can join a room the other hosts or send a friend request. They can’t watch games you play in. Games you’re already in together carry on. Reporting: you can report someone’s profile, a chat message or a room. Choose Report on it, pick a reason and add details if you like. Reports are private both ways. They never learn who reported them, and you won’t see the outcome.
Open Friends, press Message on a friend’s row and say hi. Only friends can message each other, messages stay between the two of you, and a block from either side closes the conversation.
documents.s: How do you message a friend?

documents.t: Yes. In Settings, under Your data, Download my data gives you one file with everything tied to your account: profile, settings, stats, coins, collection, badges, plan history, payments, friends, blocks, game history and messages to the team. Rent Party counts anonymous use of the game to make it better. The details are in the Privacy Policy.

From Settings, or on the Delete account page. You confirm with Google, and the account is deleted at once and can’t be undone. We email you when it’s done. To keep a copy of your data, download it first. Deleted at once: your profile, cloud saves, saved replays, friends, blocks, coins, collection, daily-challenge progress and push subscriptions, voice recordings and AI allowance counts. A paid plan ends with the account. What stays: finished online games keep your seat as “Former player”. Payment records stay only as long as tax law requires, with no game data. Reports you made or received keep an anonymous id. A recap you asked for stays with its game for the rest of the table, with no link to you. Online games still running or paused count as a forfeit for you, and the rest of the table plays on. If you own a Family plan, make another member its owner first, or the Family ends with your account and its members go back to their own plans. The Delete account page lists everything that’s deleted and everything that stays.
documents.s: How do you delete your account?

documents.t: Stuck on a rule halfway through a trade, or wondering where last night’s game got away from you? Rent Party’s AI features are for that, and each one runs only when you press its button or switch it on. The game plays the same without any of them. The CPU characters play by the game’s own rules whichever switches you choose. Fresh lines change what they say. Never how they play.

Five, and each one waits for you: the help assistant, game recaps, trade reads, fresh table-talk lines and voice recordings. Here is where each lives and what it hands back. Feature Where you find it What you get Help assistant Ask a question on the game’s Help page, or in a game’s pause menu An answer from these docs and the Help page, naming the pages it used Game recap Write the recap, under How it went, on a finished online game’s results and on its replay One short story of the game, the same for everyone who played Trade read Read this trade, in the trade window of any game What the deal does to color sets, rent and bucks, with a line of advice Fresh table-talk lines Fresh lines for each game, in Settings New lines for the CPU characters, written for that game Voice recordings Ask by voice on the Help page, the mic button on a phone, or Say your offer in the trade window A question, a message to the team or a trade offer, which you check before it’s sent

It answers only from the Rent Party docs and the game’s Help page, and under each answer From these pages names the pages it used, so you can open one and check. An answer can still be wrong. The page it names is the one that counts. On the game’s Help page, choose Ask a question. In a game, the pause menu has the same button. Type your question, or pick an example like “How do I get out of Jail?” Ask it the way you’d ask a friend across the table. When no page covers your question, it says so and offers Message the team. That one doesn’t count toward today’s questions. How do I reach the team? says what to include.
documents.s: How does the help assistant work?

documents.t: A recap is one short story of a finished online game: who won, how many rounds it took and how close it got. If you played in the game, you’ll find How it went on its results page and on its replay, right below the page’s first card. Choose Write the recap. It’s written once from the game’s moves, and everyone who sat at that table reads the same one. Only the player who writes it uses a recap from their month’s allowance. Reading one that’s already written costs nothing, so nobody at the table has to race to it, and anyone can read it again before the rematch. Recaps need an online game. Games played on one device don’t get one, and neither do guests. A recap stays with its game.

Build a trade in the trade window, then choose Read this trade. The game works out what the deal does: which color sets each side completes or breaks up; the rent at stake on the deeds that change hands; how many bucks each side holds after the deal. Our writing service then turns those facts into a short piece of advice, such as “This hands Maya a full set, so their rent doubles on every street there with no buildings. Ask for more bucks, or keep that deed back.” It’s advice only. The offer is yours. It still sends whether you read the trade or not. Put something on at least one side first: an empty trade has nothing to read.
documents.s: How does a trade read work?

documents.t: The CPU characters chat when something happens at the table: a buy, a rent bill, a trade, a trip to Jail. Land on Bea’s street and you’ll hear about it. “You’re on my street? Lovely.” Three switches in Settings, under Appearance, decide how you hear them: Switch Starts What it does CPU characters speak out loud On A voice on your browser or phone reads their lines, each character with their own pitch and pace. Show their lines On A speech bubble by the character’s seat, for about 3 seconds. Fresh lines for each game Off Our writing service writes new lines for the game. Left off, the characters use their own written lines, all on your device. Turn the first two off and the CPU characters play quietly. In a game, the pause menu has a CPU voices switch for speaking out loud, so you don’t have to leave the table to quiet them. Signed in, your switches follow you to every device. No voice on your browser or phone? You’ll see the bubbles without sound. The first time you play CPU characters on a device, a small card beside the table offers fresh lines. Choose Turn on or Not now; Settings changes it any time. Fresh lines come from an allowance for each game, counted by the day in pass-and-play and CPU games, and when they run out, the characters go back to their own written lines. The six rivals are on the CPU characters page.

Say it instead of typing. On the game’s Help page, choose Ask by voice. On a phone, the round mic button sits at the bottom right on Home, Games and Help. In a game’s trade window, choose Say your offer. Press Start and talk for up to 2 minutes. The first time, your phone or browser asks for the microphone. Rent Party listens only while the sheet says Recording and lets go of the microphone when you stop. Choose Stop and check, and your recording becomes one of these: a question for the help assistant; a message to the team, with its topic; as a guest, you add your email address so the team can reply; a trade offer, which opens in the trade window for you to change. Nothing is sent until you press the button. Rather type? When the microphone is blocked, or a recording doesn’t work, Type instead takes you to the typed version.

Not for long. Under What we heard, Delete this recording removes it at once. Otherwise the recording, the words heard in it and what it became are deleted within 24 hours. Other players never hear it, and never see its words. The privacy page has what happens to a voice recording.

Only what that feature needs, and only when you ask. Our server sends each request, not your device, so none of them carries your name, your email address or the random id behind your account. The help assistant: your question, and the text of the docs pages closest to it. A game recap: the game’s results, like each seat’s rank, net worth and the rent it paid and collected. Seats go as “Player 1”, “Player 2” or the CPU character’s name, never a display name. A trade read: what’s in the trade, and both sides’ bucks before and after. Nothing about the dice or the card decks. Fresh lines: the characters’ names and one-line sketches, and for each moment what happened and at which seat. No amounts. No players’ names. A voice recording: the audio goes to our transcription service, then what it heard, what your browser heard and the page you recorded on go to our writing service. On the website, where your words show up as you speak, your browser’s own speech service hears you too. The Android app doesn’t use one. Until it’s deleted, a recording waits as a private file with our own email and file service. Lines read aloud use only a voice on your device. Nothing is sent to read a line, and a browser or phone with no voice of its own shows the bubbles without sound. We don’t keep your question, its answer or a trade read. A recap stays with its game. The privacy page names each service and lists exactly what goes where: What do the AI features send, and where? Privacy and terms sums up the privacy page.

Spark, Pulse and Surge are the three AI levels, and yours sets how much thought goes into help answers, recaps and trade reads. Spark is quick. Pulse goes deeper. Surge goes deepest. Plan AI level Guest or Free Spark Pro Pulse, then Surge after a set number of paid months in a row, shown on the Pricing page Family Surge On Pro, only months you paid for count toward Surge, so months earned with friend invites don’t. Miss a paid month and the count starts again, though a short gap between paid months keeps the run going. Your plan page shows where you stand. A level is the highest your plan runs at. When there’s less AI credit to go round, the features can run at a lower level for a while. Plans and pricing covers the plans themselves.

Every plan includes an allowance of each feature, and Pro and Family include more. The Pricing page has the current numbers, and your plan page shows how many you’ve used. Feature Counted per Help assistant questions day Game recaps month Trade reads day Fresh table-talk lines game (a day in pass-and-play and CPU games) Voice recordings month Days and months run on UTC, so new questions can arrive at an hour that isn’t your midnight. The sheet says when. When an allowance runs out, that feature waits for the next day, month or game, and everything else carries on: the docs stay open, your trade offer still sends, and you can still type. A question the docs don’t cover doesn’t count. Neither does a request that comes back with nothing.
documents.s: How much of each feature can you use?

documents.t: Yes, all but recaps, at Spark. A guest’s allowances are worked out from the Free plan’s numbers and start fresh each day. Each sheet shows what’s left today. Before each request, a quick check makes sure you’re a person. The privacy page says what Rent Party keeps when a guest uses them.

The AI features run on a free AI credit. When it’s used up, they rest. Nothing is charged while they rest, and each sheet shows when the credit comes back. The game goes on: the help assistant points you to the docs and the team; a recap waits, because the game’s moves are kept; your trade offer still sends, without a read; voice recordings wait, and you can type; the CPU characters talk from their own written lines.
documents.s: What happens when AI is resting?

documents.t: To quiet the CPU characters, turn off CPU characters speak out loud in Settings, under Appearance, or CPU voices in the pause menu. Table talk’s other two switches sit beside the first one in Settings. The help assistant, recaps, trade reads and voice have nothing to switch off: each runs only when you press its button. To block the microphone, switch it off for Rent Party in your phone’s or browser’s settings, and the permissions page says when the microphone is used. Got a question right now? Ask the help assistant.
documents.s: How do you turn the CPU voices off?

documents.t: Take your table to a new city. Its streets and cards have local names; the rules stay the same. Coins buy looks, never luck.

Every city is a set of seven looks: street names, deed cards, card backs, banknotes, an avatar, dice and a token. Buy one at a time or complete the set, and none of them changes the rules or the luck. Look What it changes Who sees it Street names Streets, stations and cards get the city's names. Rent and rules don't change. Everyone sees it when you host Deed cards Your deed cards get the city's street-sign band, with its landmark as a watermark. Shows on your screen Card backs Card backs show the city's landmark. Only the back changes. Shows on your screen Banknotes Your bucks print as notes with the country's currency code and symbol and the city's landmark. The amounts don't change. Shows on your screen Avatar Your picture wears a city frame, with the city's landmark on its badge. Everyone at the table sees it Dice Dice in the city's colors, with its landmark on the one. Every roll stays fair. Everyone at the table sees it Token Your token on the board, stamped for the city. Everyone at the table sees it The host picks the city for the whole online table. Everyone sees its streets and cards. Complete the set charges only for the looks still missing.
documents.s: What does a city set include?

documents.t: Coins are in-app only. They can’t be withdrawn, cashed out or exchanged for money, and they have no cash value. You earn coins by playing, and on the website you can also get a coin pack. Spend them on looks in the shop, put them in at a coin table, or send some to another player. Numbers on this page They match the game’s current settings. The game’s own pages always show the latest: the shop for coin packs, and Coin tables and Send coins for those.
documents.s: Coins: coin packs, coin tables and sending coins

documents.t: From play: finishing online games, and CPU games while you’re signed in, plus badges, the daily challenge, welcome coins and confirmed friend invites. The shop’s How to earn coins list shows each one. On the website you can also get a coin pack. Every coin in and out is in your coin history.

Coin packs are on the website only. Sign in with Google, open the shop and choose Coin packs. The Android app has no coin packs. Pack Coins $5 1,000 coins $10 2,000 coins $15 3,000 coins $20 4,000 coins $50 10,000 coins $100 20,000 coins Or pick Your own amount: any whole number of dollars from $21, at the same 200 coins per dollar. The shop tells you how many coins that is before you go on. Checkout goes through our payment partner. Once the payment goes through, the coins land in your coin history in a moment. Every purchase is final, coin packs included. The Terms cover coin packs.

Everyone at a coin table puts in the same table fee. The last one standing collects the table. Open Coin tables and pick a table. Fees run from 50 to 1,000 coins, and each card shows its fee, its seats, how many are looking now, what the table collects, and the reputation level it opens at, if any. Choose Join for the fee on its card, then Put in the fee to confirm. Your fee leaves your balance when the game starts. Nothing is held while you wait. Leave the table before the game starts and no coins are taken. To join you need enough coins for the fee, and you can sit at one table at a time. Coin tables count toward your rating and reputation.

What happens Where the fees go One player is left standing They collect the table: every fee put in. The game ends on highest net worth, by a limit or by agreement The seats tied for the highest net worth share the table. Any coins left over from the split go one each, in finishing order. You leave, or go offline too long, after the first roll Your fee stays with the table. The game is called off before the first roll Every fee goes back. Nobody can collect the table Every fee goes back. The 2-minute offline rule applies at coin tables, as in every live game.

A coin challenge is a coin table for you and your friends. Everyone puts in the same fee, and the last one standing collects the table. On Coin tables, under Coin challenge: Pick the table fee and who’s invited. A coin challenge seats up to 8 people, you included, and shows how many coins the table holds. Choose Send the challenge. Each friend chooses Put in the fee, or Not this time. Once everyone invited has answered, choose Open the table. Everyone puts in the fee when the game starts. Before anyone rolls, you can Call it off, and every fee goes back to whoever put it in. You can also send a coin challenge to one friend from Online now, or find a coin table match there.

Open Send coins. You can send coins to anyone in Rent Party. Type the first 3 letters of their name, or their whole invite code, and choose Find. Pick an amount, in tens: 10, 20, 30 and up. Choose Review, confirm, then Send. Rule What it means Transfer fee 10% of what you send. Send 100 and they receive 90. Daily limit Up to 10,000 coins sent and 10,000 received each day. The count starts again at midnight UTC. Confirming Your transfer PIN, or signing in again when your last sign-in is more than 15 minutes old. Signed in recently? No PIN is needed that time. A sent transfer can’t be taken back. Both of you see it in your coin history. You can’t send coins to someone you’ve blocked or who blocked you, or while your account is suspended.

In Settings, under Online and coins, choose Set a PIN. Use 4 to 6 digits, and don’t use your birthday. If your last sign-in isn’t recent, you sign in again first. The PIN confirms every coin transfer you send. Too many wrong tries locks it for a while, and you can still sign in again to confirm a transfer. You can change or remove it in the same place. Without a PIN, Rent Party asks you to sign in again.
documents.s: How do you set a transfer PIN?

documents.t: Community is for game-night stories, rematch calls and the odd building tip from the people you play with.

Under Write a post, say how game night went. You can use bold, italics and a bulleted list, and link a game or a table record. Choose who sees it, then Post. There’s a character limit, and the box counts as you type.
You choose for each post: Who sees it Means Friends Your friends, on their Friends tab. Everyone Everyone on Rent Party, on the Everyone tab. Each post shows which one it went to.
Choose Like on a post. Choose Comment to read the comments and write your own, then Reply. You can delete your own posts and comments. A deleted post has an Undo.
documents.s: How do likes and comments work?

documents.t: Open the post’s menu, the More button, and choose: Report, for a post or a comment that breaks the rules in the Terms. Pick a reason and add details if you like. Block, with the person’s name. Posts from people you’ve blocked never show here. If the team hides one of your posts, you see why on the post, and only you can see it.
documents.s: How do you report a post or block someone?

documents.t: Your words stay in the box with the reason under it: You see Why You’ve posted a lot this hour. There’s an hourly limit on posts and comments. Try again a little later. That didn’t go through. Try different words. It has a word Rent Party doesn’t allow. Posting and comments are off while your chat is muted. A mute covers posts too, until the date shown. Posting is off while your account is suspended. A suspended account can’t post. That post isn’t here any more. It was deleted while you were writing. Friends, blocks and reports covers blocking and reporting everywhere else in the game.
documents.s: Why didn’t your post go through?

documents.t: Quick answers to the questions players ask most. Still stuck? Ask the help assistant on the game’s Help page, typed or out loud, or write to the team. Numbers on this page They match the game’s current settings. The game’s own Help page always shows the latest.
Choose Sign in and pick your Google account. Google is the only sign-in, so there’s no Rent Party password to forget.

Online games live on our server, so they follow your account. Pass-and-play and CPU games save on your device after every move. Signed in, you can keep them as cloud saves too. Clearing the browser’s site data, or uninstalling the app, deletes games saved only on that device. A cloud save isn’t affected.
Yes. Sign in with the same Google account and your online games, cloud saves, coins and collection are waiting, while a game saved only on one device stays on that device.

Open it from Games and tap I’m ready. Play resumes when everyone at the table is ready. After 14 days paused, whoever’s ready can start a 48-hour final call; anyone still not ready when it ends forfeits. If nobody starts one, the game closes, unrated, after 21 days. Pausing a game has the full picture.
documents.s: Our online game is paused. How do we start again?

documents.t: On the Rent Party website, from Pricing. A card payment takes effect as soon as it goes through. The team checks a payment you report by hand, and it takes effect the day they confirm it. We email you when a reported payment is in review and again when it’s confirmed. Plans and pricing covers both ways to pay.
documents.s: How do I buy Pro or Family?

documents.t: A push needs notifications allowed on that device and switched on in Settings, and it waits until your quiet hours end before it reaches you. Every alert still lands in your Inbox, so check there first. Game alerts don’t come by email.
documents.s: Why didn’t I get an alert for my turn?

documents.t: From Settings, or on the Delete account page. You confirm with Google, and the account is deleted at once and can’t be undone. We email you when it’s done. The Delete account page lists what goes and what stays.
documents.s: How do I delete my account?

documents.t: You can report someone’s profile, a chat message or a room: choose Report on it, pick a reason and add details if you like. Reports are private both ways. They never learn who reported them, and you won’t see the outcome. You can also block them from their profile.
Not in an app store yet. Rent Party runs in a current browser on phones, tablets and computers, iPhone and iPad included, with the same game, the same account and the same table everywhere.

Yes. On the game’s Help page, choose Ask a question, or in a game, open the pause menu and choose it there. The help assistant answers only from these docs and the Help page, and it names the pages it used so you can check. Rather talk? Choose Ask by voice, say your question and check the words before it’s asked. AI features and voice has the details.
documents.s: Can I ask the game a question?

documents.t: Tell us what happened, or what you’d like to see. The form on the game’s Help page goes straight to the Rent Party team. Pick what it’s about: My account, Something’s broken, A game question, An idea, Plans and payments, or Something else. You can say it, too. Choose Ask by voice on the Help page and tell us what you’d like the team to know. You check the message before anything is sent, and the recording is deleted within 24 hours. Writing about a payment or an error? Paste the reference from the email or the error screen. Signed in, any reply comes to your Inbox and to your email. Spotted a mistake in these docs? Open an issue on the docs repository.
documents.s: How do I reach the team?

documents.t: They’re the computer opponents, each with a name and a personality, and you can play them on Easy, Normal, Hard or Expert. Begin on Easy. Move up whenever you like.

Every rival talks back, and one of them holds grudges. You can hear them out loud, too: table talk has the switches. Rival Plays like Best at Says Sunny Buys first, plans later. Easy “Is that one for sale? I’ll take it.” Captain Moss Collects stations like ships in bottles. Normal “All aboard. That’s my station.” Lulu Will trade you anything, twice. Normal “Utility for your street? Final offer. Probably.” Auntie Fern Counts every buck twice. Sometimes three times. Hard “Slow and steady buys the street.” Bea Bakes cookies, builds hotels. Hard “You’re on my street? Lovely.” Pip Never forgets an auction. Expert “You outbid me. I’ll remember that.”

Choose CPU characters when you start a game, then add them at the Players step. Up to 5 CPU characters can join one game, each with a difficulty you pick, and each character plays their own token. CPU games need no account and no connection, and the game saves on your device after every move. Play signed in and they earn coins too. A CPU game pauses any time, so a practice round can wait while you check a rule on the rules page. Get a round in before game night. Practice against a CPU character.
documents.s: How do you play against them?

documents.t: Before a game starts, pick a preset or switch house rules on one at a time. They’re set at the House rules step when you start a game. Numbers on this page They match the game’s current settings. The game’s own How to play page always shows the latest.

Preset What it sets Official The classic rules, with every house rule off. Classic family The piggy bank, the Start-landing bonus and trades any time. Quick The short game described under winning. Tournament Official, with turn and decision timers always enforced.

House rule What it does Piggy bank Taxes, fees and every card payment to the bank go in, repairs included, and whoever lands on Town Square takes it all. Start-landing bonus An extra 200 bucks for landing exactly on Start. Turn-only trading You can only trade on your own turn. Game length limit A set number of rounds or minutes, then the highest net worth wins. No auctions A street nobody buys stays with the bank. Starting bucks and salary Choose your own amounts. City-tax choice Land on City tax and pay either 200 bucks or 10% of your net worth, and you have to pick one before you count. Sealed bids For live and local games, as the auction section explains. Around one device, everyone types a bid in secret, passing the device between bids. Quick deal Everyone starts with 2 random deeds from the bank. If your family always piled the taxes in the middle of the board and handed the pile to whoever stopped on the quiet corner, the piggy bank is that rule.
documents.s: Which house rules can you switch on?

documents.t: Only Official or Tournament. A rated online game counts toward your rating when every seat is a person. Online play explains ratings.
documents.s: Which rules can a rated game use?

documents.t: Every name that’s ours, in one place.

Rent Party word What it means street A deed in a color set. Houses and hotels go here. deed The card that proves you own a street, station or utility. station · utility The 4 stations and 2 utilities you can own. Start The first corner, where you collect your salary. Jail · just passing by The second corner, and what you are when an ordinary roll lands you there. Town Square The rest corner, home of the piggy bank house rule. Go to jail The fourth corner. It sends you to Jail. City tax · Party tax The two tax spaces. Lucky Break · Neighborhood Mail The two card decks. Jail pass The card that gets you out of Jail. Keep it or trade it. bucks The play money in every game. coins Earned in online and CPU games, or got in a coin pack on the website. Spent on tokens, boards and dice skins, put in at coin tables, or sent to another player. In-app only, with no cash value, and separate from bucks. Coins has the details. Kettleford The board that comes with the game.

Rent Party word What it means CPU characters The computer opponents, each with a name and a personality. Meet them. game invite An invite to a game room: a link, a QR code or a 6-character room code. Family invite An invite to a seat on a Family plan, sent by email. friend invite An invite to Rent Party itself. Confirmed ones earn coins, a badge and months of Pro.

Local and CPU games pause any time, and they’re still there after you close the app. An online game pauses only when everyone at the table agrees. It resumes once everyone’s ready. Dinner’s on the table? Pause. Numbers on this page They match the game’s current settings. The game’s own How to play page always shows the latest.
When a paused game resumes, you’re back on the same turn at the same table, with every deed exactly where you left it. Signed-in players can continue on another device.
documents.s: What happens when a game resumes?

documents.t: Choose Ask to pause. Everyone has to agree, so the game asks the table. Everyone has to say yes before the vote’s time runs out, and one Keep playing ends the vote. Play carries on meanwhile. If not everyone agrees, or the vote runs out of time, the game goes on. When everyone says yes, the game’s paused, and your seat’s saved.
documents.s: How do you pause an online game?

documents.t: Open the game from Games and tap I’m ready. Play resumes the moment everyone’s ready.

A paused online game waits 14 days, and your seat’s saved the whole time. After that, the players who are ready can start a 48-hour final call. Anyone who still isn’t ready when it ends forfeits, their deeds go to auction, and the game resumes with everyone else. If everyone else forfeits, the game is yours. If nobody starts a final call, the game closes, unrated, after 21 days.
documents.s: How long does a paused online game wait?

documents.t: Leaving an online game counts as a forfeit, paused or not: their deeds go back to the bank and are auctioned, and the rest of the table plays on. Leave a paused game and your deeds go to auction when play resumes. If you need to step away, ask the table for a pause instead. A friend who just stops taking turns falls under the missed-turn rule.
documents.s: What happens if a friend leaves an online game?

documents.t: You roll two dice, buy the unowned streets you land on, trade for full color sets, and build houses and hotels so the rent on your streets keeps climbing. The game runs the bank, and play can pause and pick up again over several evenings. The last player who isn’t bankrupt wins. Numbers on this page They match the game’s current settings. The game’s own How to play page always shows the latest.

Yes — buying, auctions, rent, building, mortgages, Jail and bankruptcy follow the classic property-trading rules, with optional house rules you switch on before a game. Nobody has to be the banker this time. Some names are our own. Rent Party names lists every one.
documents.s: Does Rent Party use the classic rules?

documents.t: Pick how you’re playing: online with friends, around one phone or tablet, or against CPU characters. Then switch on any house rules you want before the first roll. A game seats 2 to 8 players. Each of you starts with 1,500 bucks and picks a token. Someone always has a favorite.
documents.s: How do you set up a game?

documents.t: Every turn starts with the tumble of two dice: you move your token clockwise by the total, and the space where it stops decides what happens next. Each time you pass Start or land on it, the bank pays you a salary of 200 bucks. Doubles mean you go again. Finish this move first, including the choice to buy or auction. Roll doubles a third time in the same turn and you go to Jail instead. Nobody stays that lucky.

You can buy it at the price printed on its deed, or turn it down and it goes straight to auction. Same for stations and utilities. Turning it down isn’t the end of it. You can still bid, and you might get it for less than the printed price. Or you might watch Priya do exactly that.
documents.s: What happens when you land on an unowned street?

documents.t: If the player who lands on an unowned street doesn’t buy it, it goes to auction straight away, everyone — that player included — can bid, and the highest bid wins. You can’t bid more bucks than you’re holding. Pass when the price gets silly. If nobody bids at all, the street stays with the bank, so the next person to land on it gets the same choice to buy it or send it to auction. In a game over days, auctions are always sealed bids. One bid each, highest wins. Live and local games can switch sealed bids on as a house rule. Nothing makes a street look better than somebody else bidding on it.
documents.s: How do auctions work when nobody buys a street?

documents.t: Land on a street, station or utility someone else owns and you pay them rent. You land on You pay A street The rent on its deed. Once the owner has the full color set, it doubles on every street in the set with no buildings, even if others in the set have houses. Houses and hotels raise it to the amounts the deed lists. A station 25 bucks if the owner has 1 station · 50 for 2 · 100 for 3 · 200 for all 4 A utility 4 times your dice roll if the owner has 1 utility · 10 times if they have both A mortgaged deed Nothing If an 8 lands you on a utility whose owner has both, you pay 80 bucks. Owner in Jail? Rent’s still due. Maya just landed on one of your stations, and you own all 4. That’s 200 bucks, Maya.

You go to Jail by landing on Go to jail, by drawing a card that sends you there, or by rolling doubles 3 times in one turn. Three ways out: pay 50 bucks, use a Jail pass, or roll doubles. Roll your way out and you move by that roll, with no extra roll after it. After 3 tries without doubles, you pay the 50 bucks and move. Jail stops your token. It doesn’t stop your deeds: you still collect rent, build and trade while you’re there. Land on Jail with an ordinary roll and you’re just passing by.

They’re the two card decks, with 16 cards each. Land on one of their spaces and you draw a card, which can move you around the board, pay you, charge you, or bill you for repairs on every house and hotel you own. Draw a Jail pass and you can keep it until you need it, or trade it. Some cards are a gift. A repairs card isn’t, if you’ve been building.
documents.s: What are Lucky Break and Neighborhood Mail?

documents.t: Town Square is the rest corner: nothing happens there unless the piggy bank house rule is on. City tax costs 200 bucks, and Party tax costs 100.
documents.s: What happens on Town Square and the tax spaces?

documents.t: Own every street in a color set, then build evenly across it, one house at a time; a hotel replaces 4 houses. You buy each house from the bank at the price printed on its street’s deed. No street can get its second house until every other street in the set has its first, and the same goes for each house after that. Your neighborhood grows houses first. Then hotels. Stations and utilities never take buildings. The bank has 32 houses and 12 hotels in all. When they run out, nobody can build. Holding 4 houses on every street of a set keeps them out of everyone else’s hands, too. Selling works the same way in reverse: buildings go back to the bank at half price, evenly across the set.
documents.s: How do you build houses and hotels?

documents.t: You can trade streets, stations, utilities, bucks and Jail passes with any player, at any time, unless the turn-only trading house rule is on. Make an offer. They can take it or turn it down. While you owe a payment, you can only trade to raise the money for it. You can’t trade a street while any street in its color set has buildings. Sell them back to the bank first. Mortgaged deeds can change hands too, and the mortgage section explains the 10% the receiver pays. The best deals start with one street that someone needs to finish a color set, and with everyone else at the table knowing exactly how badly.

Mortgage a deed and the bank pays you half its printed price. The deed stays yours, but it charges no rent until you pay it back. It’s just taking a nap. Paying it back costs the mortgage plus 10%: every 100 bucks you borrowed costs 110. You can only mortgage a street when no street in its color set has buildings. Sell those first. If a mortgaged deed changes hands, whoever receives it pays the 10% straight away.

You raise the money first — sell buildings back to the bank at half price or mortgage deeds — and you only go bankrupt if that still isn’t enough. The same goes for anything else you owe. Trading counts too. A friend might give you bucks for a deed. Count your houses before you count yourself out. Owe another player and still can’t cover it? They get everything you have left. If it’s the bank you owe, your deeds go to auction. Either way, your game ends there and everyone else plays on.
documents.s: What happens when you can’t pay rent?

documents.t: Be the last player who isn’t bankrupt. Until then, the leader is fair game. Quick mode is different: everyone starts with 2 random deeds, and after 20 rounds the highest net worth wins. Net worth is your bucks, plus your unmortgaged deeds at their printed price, plus your buildings at what they cost, with mortgaged deeds counted at half.

As long as your table wants. Quick mode ends after a set number of rounds and the richest player wins, and a full game can stretch over several evenings with pauses in between. Nobody has to stay up till 1 a.m. to see who wins anymore. Pausing a game shows how. Rather learn by playing? Practice against a CPU character.
documents.s: How long does a game take?

documents.t: Learn the game is the real Rent Party game screen on a demo table, with a coach that walks you through every control in 16 steps and then takes you to set up a practice game. Open it at rentparty.aoneahsan.com/learn. Nothing on the demo table is saved.

Every control on the game screen, in the order a turn uses them: This is the table: a demo game called Sunday night, and you’re Noor, the rocket. Who’s playing: one chip per player, showing their bucks and how many deeds they hold. Roll the dice: doubles mean you go again, and 3 in a row send you to Jail. Buy a street: buy it at the printed price, or turn it down and it goes to auction. Bid at auction: everyone can bid, you included. A pass is final. Latest move: who paid whom; press it for the whole game log. Your deeds: press any street on the board to read its deed. Manage what you own: every build and every mortgage happens here. Houses and hotels: own the whole color set and build evenly. A hotel comes after 4 houses. Mortgage and pay back: the bank pays you half the printed price, and paying it back costs that plus 10%. Trade: offer deeds or bucks to anyone at the table. The game log: every move so far, newest at the bottom. Moments: the big ones pop up on the table, then leave by themselves. End your turn: the dice pass to the next player. Pause the game: pause saves your seat. You’re ready: come back any time, or play a practice game.
documents.s: What does Learn the game show?

documents.t: Press Learn the game in the site header, in the footer’s Play group or in your account menu, whichever is closest when you want a refresher. In a game, open the pause menu and choose How the game screen works. It covers the game screen only. Every other page has a tour of its own, from the button in the header. The first time you open a game, a short note offers it: Your first roll can wait. Learn the game screen first. Choose Show me to start. The note appears once in each browser and once for your account, so a second device won’t show it again.
documents.s: How do I open Learn the game?

documents.t: Yes, at any step. Next and Back move one step, and All steps lists all 16 so you can jump straight to one. Skip or Close ends it and takes you to How to play. Escape does the same. Each step puts a ring around one control, and the table stays live, so you can press what the step points at and see what it does.
documents.s: Can I skip steps or leave?

documents.t: No. Sunday night is a demo with Noor, Maya, Sam and Pip the CPU character at the table, and nothing you do there is saved, so roll and build all you like.
documents.s: Is anything on the demo table saved?

documents.t: Play a practice game takes you to set up a practice game against a CPU character, where the next roll counts. Ready when you are. Learn the game.
documents.s: What happens at the last step?

documents.t: Update now, or Rent Party asks you to the next time you open it.
Update now, or Rent Party asks you to the next time you open it.
The new version we told you about is needed now. Update to keep playing. This one can’t wait. Update Rent Party to keep playing. Your games are saved. You’ll pick up right where you left off.
That didn’t finish. Try again, or get the new version from the store.
Online now shows who’s around right now. Challenge a friend, invite someone to your room, or let Rent Party find you a match. Online now needs you to be signed in.

Signed-in players who are online, with friends first and everyone else after. When the list is long, it shows the first part of it, friends always first. Each card shows what that person is doing: Status Means Around Online, not in a game. In a game Playing now. Looking for a match Waiting for a match. Every card carries the person’s reputation level. From a card you can Challenge, Invite to room or Add friend.
In Settings, under Online and coins, switch off Show me on Online now. When it’s off, nobody sees you on the Online now list, and you can still see them. Matches still find you when you look for one.

Choose Challenge on their card, then pick what kind of game: Kind What it is Friendly No coins. Just the game. Coin challenge You both put in the same table fee. Coin challenges has the details. Choose Send challenge. Changed your mind? Take it back. Your friend gets the challenge and chooses Accept or Not now. Accepting opens your room. There’s one challenge between the two of you at a time, and an hourly limit on how many you send.
documents.s: How do you challenge a friend?

documents.t: Choose Invite to room on their card. They get an invite in their inbox and join your waiting room. No waiting room yet? Choose Start a room first.
documents.s: How do you invite someone to your room?

documents.t: Rent Party pairs you with someone at a similar reputation level. Under Find a match, pick Friendly, or Coin table and a table fee. Choose Find a match. Rent Party looks for someone near your level, and widens the levels if it’s still looking. When a match is found, you see their level and a countdown. Choose Accept, or Skip. Stop looking ends the search. If the match times out, nothing is taken, and you can look again whenever you like. A coin table can open at a set reputation level, and you need enough coins for its fee. With a coin table, you each put in the fee when the game starts.
documents.s: How does Find a match work?

documents.t: Start a room and share the link. Friends get a nudge when you open one. Online play covers rooms and invites.

Start a room for your friends, or join one with a code. Same table, any distance. Online play needs an account. Sign in with Google to start or join a room. Numbers on this page They match the game’s current settings. The game’s own How to play page always shows the latest.

Mode How it plays Live Everyone plays at the same time, with 90-second turns. Over days Everyone takes a turn when they can, with a deadline of 8, 12, 24 or 48 hours per turn. In a live room, everyone’s on at once, like the old Fridays. In a game over days, the room picks the deadline and you get a nudge when it’s your move. Take your turn on the bus, or right before bed. Its auctions always use sealed bids.
documents.s: Live room or game over days?

documents.t: On Play online, under Start a room, choose Live or Over days and who can find it, then choose New room. Set up the players, board and house rules as for any game. The last step is Create room. Who can find it Means Invite only Only people with your link or code. Friends Listed for your friends. Anyone else needs your link or code. Anyone Listed under public rooms for anyone to join. The host’s game settings also cover the seats, the turn deadline for a game over days, whether people can watch, and whether the game is rated. Only the host can change these. Your plan sets how many live games and games over days you can be in at once. When you reach it, finish one to start another. Plans and pricing explains the limits.
documents.s: How do you start a room?

documents.t: Send each friend a game invite: a link, a QR code or a 6-character room code. The invite works while the room waits in its lobby, 24 hours by default. A friend with a code joins from Start a game, under Join a room, which takes the 6-character code, or the whole invite or Watch link. Play online has Join with a code too. If a code doesn’t work, the game says why: You see What to do No room has that code. Check it and try again. That room’s lobby has closed. Ask for a new invite. That room is full. Ask the host for a seat. That game has already started. Ask the host for an invite to the next one, or for the Watch link to follow it.

Everyone seated taps I’m ready. Start opens once everyone seated is ready, you need at least 2 seats filled, and the host starts the game. The host can remove someone from the room, and their seat opens up. If the host leaves, the role passes to the next person seated. If nobody else is seated, leaving cancels the room and the invite stops working.

Miss a turn in either mode and the game plays it for you with safe moves. That counts as a strike. In a live room, 3 strikes in a row is a forfeit. Over days, 2 in a row is enough. Each decision has its own timer. When one runs out: Time runs out on What happens Your turn The game plays your turn with safe moves. That counts as a strike. Buying a street The deed goes to auction. That counts as a strike. A bid You pass. That counts as a strike. A choice The game makes the safe choice for you. That counts as a strike. Raising money you owe The game raises the money for you: buildings are sold first, then deeds are mortgaged. You’re bankrupt only if that still isn’t enough. Running out of time counts as a strike. A trade offer The offer closes. No strike for that. Connection lost? Your timer keeps running, so reconnect when you can. In a live game, you have 2 minutes to come back: What if someone goes offline? explains.
documents.s: What if you miss a turn?

documents.t: Nobody sees your bid before the reveal, not even spectators. Your bid is sealed until everyone has bid or time runs out. Bids are revealed at the deadline, and if you haven’t bid by then, you pass, which counts as a strike.
Anyone at the table can ask, and everyone has to agree. Pausing a game covers the vote, starting again and the final call.
documents.s: How do you pause an online game?

documents.t: Anyone at the table can choose End by agreement to end the game now. If everyone agrees before the vote’s time runs out, the highest net worth wins. If not everyone agrees, or the vote runs out of time, the game goes on. A rated game still counts toward ratings when it ends this way.
documents.s: How does End by agreement work?

documents.t: Leaving an online game counts as a forfeit, paused or not. Their deeds go to auction, and the rest of the table plays on. Pausing a game has the details.

In a live game, a player who’s offline for 2 minutes leaves the game. Paused games and games over days aren’t affected. While the clock runs, their seat shows Offline and a countdown, and a banner tells the table. If they’re back in time, they play on. If not: Players left What happens 2 The other player wins. More than 2 The game goes on, and their deeds go to auction. If the room uses the No auctions house rule, the deeds go back to the bank, as that rule says. A rated game counts it as a loss, like any forfeit. To keep it fair, the clock starts when the game starts or resumes, it never runs for a CPU character, and it runs only while someone else at the table is still connected. If Rent Party itself goes down, nobody loses a seat to it.

Yes, when the host lets people watch. Spectators join with the Watch link, and your plan sets how many can watch a game you host. Spectators see the board, never anyone’s sealed bids, and chat is for the table.

Say something to the table with typed messages, quick chat and emotes. If typed chat is off, quick chat and emotes still work. Choose Report message on any message that breaks the chat rules in the Terms.

A game can be rated when every seat is a person and it uses Official or Tournament rules. A forfeit in a rated game counts as a rated loss. Your games count toward your rating either way. The leaderboard shows you only after you switch it on in your profile.
One winner, one result card, one tap to rematch. When the host offers a rematch, choose Join rematch to take your seat again.
If Rent Party says online play is full right now, your local games still work. If it says games over days are paused right now, live rooms still work.
documents.s: What if online play is busy?

documents.t: Free is the whole game. You get every mode and every house rule on Free. Pro and Family raise limits on things that cost us money to run, AI allowances included. They also raise the level the AI features run at. Every difference between the plans is a limit or the AI level, never a game feature. The Pricing page shows the current prices and limits, with the date they were set.
Yes — the whole game is free to play; Pro and Family raise limits, like how many online games you can run at once. They raise the AI level too.

Plan Price In short Free Costs nothing The whole game, start to finish, with AI at Spark. Pro Monthly Higher limits, for you, with AI at Pulse, then Surge. Family Per seat, monthly The highest limits, for everyone on the plan, with AI at Surge. Compare plans for the current prices.

Higher limits, and a higher AI level. You can run more live games and games over days at once, save more games to the cloud, keep more replays longer, let more people watch the games you host and use the AI features more. The Pricing page compares the plans on these rows: Live online games at once Games over days at once Cloud-save slots Saved replays Replays kept for Spectators per game you host Friends AI level Help assistant questions a day Game recaps a month Trade reads a day Fresh table-talk lines a game (a day in local games) Voice recordings a month Paid months in a row to reach Surge No token, board, dice skin, frame or CPU character comes with a plan. Looks are earned with coins on every plan.
documents.s: What do Pro and Family add?

documents.t: Your AI level sets how much thought goes into help answers, recaps and trade reads. Free runs at Spark. Pro runs at Pulse, then Surge after a set number of paid months in a row, shown on the Pricing page. Family runs at Surge for everyone on the plan. AI features and voice explains the levels and how Pro reaches Surge.
documents.s: What do the AI levels mean?

documents.t: Family is paid per seat, you included, and the Pricing page shows how many seats it covers. Whoever buys it sends the other members a Family invite by email, and every member signs in with their own Rent Party account and gets Family’s limits.
documents.s: How does the Family plan work?

documents.t: On the Rent Party website, from Pricing. There are two ways to pay, and checkout shows which you can use. By card. Choose Pay by card. You pay on our payment partner’s page, and they email you a confirmation. Your plan starts as soon as the payment goes through. A payment you report. When checkout offers it, you make the payment another way and then report it there, with its reference. The team checks a payment you report by hand. Your plan starts the day it’s confirmed. We email you when a reported payment is in review and again when it’s confirmed. Plans are sold only on the Rent Party website, and the Android app shows the plan you’re on without selling one. Once your plan starts, it works everywhere you sign in, the Android app included. A plan doesn’t renew on its own. “How do you buy a plan?” in the Terms covers buying in full.
documents.s: How do you buy a plan?

documents.t: When your card payment goes through. A payment you report starts your plan once the Rent Party team confirms it by hand, and either way the confirming email gives the date it runs until: one month for each month you paid for. If a payment you report isn’t confirmed, your plan stays as it was and we email you. Write to us from the Help page if neither comes.

Your account moves to Free, and we email you before that happens. Nothing is deleted in the move. Online games already running play on to the end, and Free’s limits only block starting new ones. Cloud saves and replays above Free’s slots become read-only until a plan covers them again, and each replay keeps the expiry date it already had.
documents.s: What happens when a plan ends?

documents.t: Yes. Confirmed friend invites earn you months of Pro, up to a set number of months in any 365 days, and the Pricing page shows the current numbers. Each invite also earns coins and a badge. An invite counts once your friend has an account and their email address is confirmed. If you’re on Pro or Family already, the reward extends your plan. Start on Free, and choose Pro when you need more room. Compare plans.
documents.s: Can you get Pro without paying?

documents.t: These are short guides to the game’s legal pages, not the pages themselves. The pages on rentparty.aoneahsan.com are the ones that apply, and each shows the date it was last updated.

We don’t sell your personal data, and you can delete your account from Settings whenever you like. The privacy page says what Rent Party does keep about you, why, which services help run the game, how long each thing stays and how you change it. A few answers from it: Rent Party shows no third-party ads. A small panel can promote the team’s own other apps. Pass-and-play and CPU games are saved only on your device. The team never receives those saves. Rent Party is for anyone aged 13 and over, and the game’s own content is family-friendly. Voice recordings, and the words heard in them, are deleted within 24 hours, or at once from the recording sheet. Other players never hear them. Community posts reach only the people you share them with, and a post or comment you delete is gone for good 30 days later. Settings decides whether you show on Online now. The AI features send only what each one needs, and only when you ask. The privacy page lists what each one sends and where, and AI features and voice sums it up. Read the privacy policy.

These terms are the rules for using Rent Party, on the website at rentparty.aoneahsan.com and in the Android app. By playing, you agree to them. They cover: who can use Rent Party; what’s free, what plans add, and how buying a plan and a Family plan work; what happens when a plan ends; what bucks and coins are worth, and what friend invites earn; how the AI features work, and what plans include of them; fair play, leaving games and missed turns; what you can say in names, rooms, chat and community posts, and how reports and blocks work; what happens when someone breaks these rules; who owns the game, and whether it can change or go offline; who’s responsible if something goes wrong, and which law applies; how you’ll know the terms changed, and how to reach the team. Read the terms.

Rent Party asks for two permissions: notifications and the microphone. Each comes only after you tap. Notifications come up when you turn alerts on. The microphone comes up when you press the mic and then Start to record, and Rent Party uses it only while you record. Say no to either and the game plays the same. Without the microphone, you type. The permissions page lists every permission the Android app and the website use, what each is for, when you’re asked and what happens if you refuse. See the permissions.

You can delete your Rent Party account at any time from Settings, on the website or in the Android app. Deletion is immediate and can’t be undone. The Delete account page lists what’s deleted at once and what stays, and Your account sums it up. Go to the Delete account page.
For privacy and legal requests, the privacy page gives the address to write to. For everything else, write to us from the Help page.
documents.s: How do you reach the team?

documents.t: Your game just ended, and its replay is already waiting: Watch replay on the results page, or under History in Games. Open it and the whole game plays back, from the table it started on to the last move. Online, pass-and-play or against CPU characters: all three.
Under History in Games, each finished game has its own row and its own Watch replay, and the results page has one the moment a game ends. Same table, same dice.
documents.s: How do I open a replay?

documents.t: The table the game started from, then every public move, step by step. You see what the players saw at the table and nothing more. Nobody’s hidden information shows up. The position reads Event number of total, so you know how far in you are.

Play starts it and Pause stops it. Speed runs at 1×, 2× or 4×. Step back and Step forward move one event, and To start and To end jump to either end. The scrubber goes anywhere in between. Drag back to the auction everyone’s still talking about.

Anyone who played in it or watched it. An online replay comes from the server and carries a fair-dice line once the game’s revealed seed has been checked against the commitment it started with: Fair dice: this game’s seed matches the commitment published when it started.
documents.s: Who can watch an online game’s replay?

documents.t: If you played in it, it’s under How it went on the game’s results page and on its replay. That is the game recap: one short story of how it went. AI features and voice has the rest.
documents.s: Where is the recap of an online game?

documents.t: An unsaved online replay is kept for a set number of days after the game ends, the same on every plan. After that it reads This replay has expired. Its results are still in Games. To keep one longer, choose Save replay. It then stays as long as your plan allows; the Replays kept for row on Plans and pricing has that period. You’ll see Saved. Kept until with the date. The Saved replays row on the same page says how many you can keep at once, and the Pricing page shows the current numbers. Full? Delete one to save another. Deleting your account deletes your saved replays at once. Your account lists everything else that goes with it.
documents.s: How long is an online replay kept?

documents.t: Yes. A game played on one device is rebuilt on that device from its own record: this device’s copy, or your account’s cloud copy if the game was saved to the cloud and you’re signed in. From this device’s copy it works signed out too. These replays have no Save replay and no fair-dice line. The replay is the device’s own copy, and its dice were rolled on the device. Want another one to watch back? Practice against a CPU character.
documents.s: Can I replay a pass-and-play or CPU game?

documents.t: Your reputation grows when you finish what you start, stay connected and come back day after day. It starts with your first online game.

Your score is out of 100, and it’s made of four parts: Part What it counts Finishing games Games you play to the end, and games you leave early. Staying connected How steady your connection is in online games. Coming back each day Your daily streak. Time on Rent Party How long you’ve had your account. Each part counts for a share of every 100 points. Your profile shows the breakdown under How your score is made, and only you see that part.

Your score sets your level, from 1 to 10. The level shows on your profile, your public player page and your card on Online now. Other players see your level and the reputation card: games finished, games left early, connection and your streaks. For them it reads as how reliably you play games to the end. Levels matter in two places: Find a match pairs you with someone at a similar level. A coin table can open at a set level, and its card shows which one.
You’ve played fewer than 5 games so far, so your level is still settling. The label goes once you’ve played 5.

Your daily streak counts the days in a row you come back to Rent Party signed in. Your reputation card shows the current streak and your longest one. Two badges come from it: Badge How you earn it A week of game nights Open Rent Party 7 days in a row. A month of game nights Open Rent Party 30 days in a row. Your badges are on Achievements.
documents.s: How does the daily streak work?

documents.t: Leaving games early and dropping out of them. A live game also ends for you if you’re offline too long: Online play has the 2-minute rule. Coin tables count toward your rating and reputation, like any other online game.

Playing on a real board over several nights? Keep the deeds, the bucks and the box in a table record, so nobody has to remember who owned what. Open Table records and choose New record. Give it a name of 2 to 40 characters, something the table will recognize, like “Kitchen table, Friday nights”.

Four steps, in order. Each change is saved and logged. Step What you enter Players Who’s at the table, 2 to 6 people, since a real board seats 6. Each has a name and a token. Link someone to their account so they can see the record and take their seat online. Only your friends can be linked. Deeds Tick each deed a person holds. Buildings and mortgages go on the street itself. Bucks Each person’s bucks, or leave it blank. Blank reads as “not entered”. The box The houses and hotels left in the box. The record tells you what the box should hold by the deeds, and Use these numbers fills them in. Your board calls a color group something else? Choose Rename on the group and use the name on your own board, 1 to 24 characters. Use our name puts it back.

Before a game can go online, everything has to add up. The record lists anything to fix, and Go to it takes you there: A deed has one owner. Buildings need the whole color group, held by one person. A group with buildings can’t have a mortgaged street. Streets in a group can differ by one building at most. The deeds can’t hold more houses or hotels than a full box. When it all adds up, you see Everything adds up.
Every entry and every edit, newest first: when, who, what changed, and the before and after. Nothing in the log can be changed or removed. Use Show to see one person’s entries.

Yes. Choose Keep as a record, and pick it up again next game night. Close this record makes it read-only for everyone. You can reopen it later, and the log stays. Signed out, records stay on this device. Sign in to share them with the people at your table.
documents.s: Can you pick it up next time?

documents.t: Under Who can see this record, choose Add a friend, then Invite. Friends you add can see the record and add entries, and every entry lands in the log. Your friend finds it under Shared with you on their Table records list, and chooses Accept or Not now. You can remove someone at any time, and they can’t see the record any more.
documents.s: How do you share a record?

documents.t: Choose Bring online on the record. Keep playing from wherever everyone is: the board starts exactly where your table left it. Only the person who started the record can bring it online. Every seat needs its person, linked to their account, and each of them needs to accept before the game can start. Pick who rolls first, then choose Start online game. Everyone gets their seat back. The deeds, buildings, bucks and box come online as recorded. The start screen shows what comes online. A seat with no bucks entered starts with the amount shown there, and both decks are shuffled fresh. It’s a friends’ game, and it’s unrated. No coins go in and none come out. The rest of online play works as usual, pausing and votes included. Once the game is online, the record shows Moved online and is read-only.
documents.s: How do you bring a game online?

documents.t: New here? Rent Party shows you around two ways. A page tour walks through the page you’re on, and How Rent Party works covers the whole game in six screens. It takes about a minute, and you can leave at any step.

Press Take a tour of this page in the header. On a phone it’s in the bar at the top of the screen. The first time you open a page that has a tour, a short note points at the button: New here? Take a quick tour of this page. Choose Show me to start, or Dismiss. The note shows once per page.
documents.s: How do I start a page tour?

documents.t: Page What the tour shows Home Every game can pause, the ways to play, how a game night goes, and the rivals Play Pick your kind of game night, pass-and-play, Join a room, Install Rent Party Your games Every game you started, sorted by how you played it Play online Start a room, join with a code, public rooms Shop Tokens, boards, dice and frames, bought with the coins you earn playing Leaderboard Where you stand, and how ratings work Profile Your table name, what you have equipped, your stats Settings Your account, alerts, how the game looks, and your data

Yes, at any step. Next and Back move one step, and All steps lists every step so you can jump straight to one. Skip tour or Close the tour ends it, and so does Escape or a press on the dimmed page. On a keyboard, the arrow keys move between steps. On a phone, each step opens as a card at the bottom of the screen.
documents.s: Can I skip steps or leave the tour?

documents.t: A quick walk through the game, six screens long: Pick your kind of game night: online with friends, pass-and-play on one phone, or CPU characters with names, personalities and opinions. Roll, buy, build: the classic property-trading rules, applied for you. Nobody has to be the banker. Haggle at the table: offer deeds, bucks or both to anyone at the table. Pause any game: life calls? Pause the game and pick it up days later. Bring your crew online: share a link, a QR code or the six-character room code. Dress up your game: coins buy looks, never luck. Open it from How Rent Party works in the site footer or in your account menu. It’s also on the last step of onboarding: New to Rent Party? See how it works. Ready to play? Start a game.
documents.s: What is How Rent Party works?
